 Materials: Titanium isopropoxide (99.996%, C12H28O4Ti), urea Published online: January 9, 2019
(99.5%, CH4N2O), and ethanol were used as precursors for the
synthesis of carbon-doped titanium dioxide. These chemicals (AR grade)
were procured from Sigma-Aldrich and used without further purification.
 Synthesis of TiO2 and Carbon-Doped TiO2 Nanoparticles: Carbon- [1] Z. Wang, Z. Tian, D. Han, F. Gu, ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces 2016,
doped TiO2 nanoparticles were synthesized by thermal decomposition 8, 5466.
method. The titanium hydroxide was first synthesized by mixing 20 mL of [2] D. Li, Y. Zhang, D. Liu, S. Yao, F. Liu, B. Wang, P. Sun, Y. Gao,
titanium isopropoxide in ethanol solution. The resultant powder (≈9.0 g) X. Chuai, G. Lu, CrystEngComm 2016, 18, 8101.
was pulverized with 1 g of urea using a mortar for 30 min. Subsequently,
 [3] A. Hussain, A. T. S. Semeano, S. I. C. J. Palma, A. S. Pina, J. Almeida,
the pulverized powder was subjected to thermal treatment in a quartz
 B. F. Medrado, A. C. C. S. Pádua, A. L. Carvalho, M. Dionísio,
crucible under a controlled nitrogen atmosphere in a tubular furnace at
 R. W. C. Li, H. Gamboa, R. V. Ulijn, J. Gruber, A. C. A. Roque,
450 °C (heating rate, 10 °C min−1) for 2 h. After the completion of the
reaction, the powder was washed with distilled water and dried in an Adv. Funct. Mater. 2017, 27, 1700803.
oven at 80 °C for 8 h. The color of dried powder was changed from white [4] D. Bekermann, A. Gasparotto, D. Barreca, C. Maccato, E. Comini,
(TiO2) to dark brown (carbon-doped TiO2). The prepared samples are C. Sada, G. Sberveglieri, A. Devi, R. A. Fischer, ACS Appl. Mater.
represented as TiO2, C20-TiO2, C40-TiO2, and C60-TiO2 corresponding to Interfaces 2012, 4, 928.
